_meta.description: Curated, evidence-backed management promise/outcome pairs for Tata Consultancy Services. Every sourceUrl is either TCS's own official investor-relations domain (tcs.com) or the official BSE/NSE exchange corporate-filing archive that hosts the exact same regulatorily-disclosed documents (bseindia.com / nsearchives.nseindia.com) -- the latter was used for records added after tcs.com began blocking direct/automated fetching behind a Cloudflare managed challenge. See companies.json notes for why coverage is PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE.

promise.statement: Management reiterated its long-standing aspirational operating margin band of 26%-28%, stating it would keep driving toward that band while continuing to invest.
promise.originalExcerpt: Growth with profitability will remain our mantra and we'll not be shy of investments but we will be driving towards the 26% to 28% (band).

outcome.explanation: FY2026 full-year operating margin was reported at 25% (up 70 bps year-on-year, a four-year high), which is close to but below the low end of the reiterated 26%-28% aspirational band. Achievement = 25 / 26 = 96.2% of the target floor, which the deterministic status thresholds classify as PARTIAL (>=70% and <100% of target).

promiseEvidence.sourceTitle: Transcript of the Q2 2025-26 Earnings Conference Call held at 1900 hrs IST on October 9, 2025
promiseEvidence.excerpt: Growth with profitability will remain our mantra and we'll not be shy of investments but we will be driving towards the 26% to 28% (band).

outcomeEvidence.sourceTitle: TCS closes FY26 with Improving Sequential Growth Momentum and Strong Deal Wins (Q4 & full-year FY2025-26 results)
outcomeEvidence.excerpt: FY26 operating margin at 25%, up 70 bps year-on-year -- the highest operating margin in the last four years.

verification.notes: Both the promise and outcome figures were independently corroborated by multiple secondary reports of the same official TCS transcript/press-release language, but the exact page number within the transcript PDF was not confirmed, so pageNumber is left null rather than guessed and evidenceConfidence is set below the 0.9+ range reserved for page-verified citations.

promise.statement: Management characterized 12.5% LTM attrition in IT services (as of the FY2024 year-end) as being within its stated comfort range of 11%-13%, indicating an intent to keep attrition within that band going forward.
promise.originalExcerpt: Our LTM attrition in IT services kept trending down throughout the year and was at 12.5% at the end of Q4, down 80 bps sequentially and in our comfort range of 11% to 13%.

outcome.explanation: FY2025 full-year (LTM) attrition in IT services was reported at 13.3%, 0.3 percentage points above the 13% upper bound of management's stated 11%-13% comfort range. Achievement = 13 / 13.3 = 97.7% of the ceiling target, which the deterministic status thresholds (>=70% and <100% of target) classify as PARTIAL -- a narrow miss of the stated ceiling, not a substantial one.

promiseEvidence.sourceTitle: Transcript of the Earnings Conference Call for the Quarter and Year Ended March 31, 2024 (BSE Filing TCS/SE/19/2024-25)
promiseEvidence.excerpt: Our LTM attrition in IT services kept trending down throughout the year and was at 12.5% at the end of Q4, down 80 bps sequentially and in our comfort range of 11% to 13%.

outcomeEvidence.sourceTitle: Transcript of the Earnings Conference Call for the Quarter and Year Ended March 31, 2025 (BSE Filing TCS/SE/13/2025-26)
outcomeEvidence.excerpt: Our workforce at the end of FY '25 was 607,979. ... Over LTM attrition was stable at 13.3%.

verification.notes: Both figures were read directly, page-by-page, from the official BSE-filed earnings-call transcript PDFs (fetched directly from bseindia.com's corpfiling archive; tcs.com itself currently returns HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare managed challenge for any non-browser client, including this project's own DocumentResearchService pipeline). 'AT_MOST 13%' is this record's schema encoding of management's stated two-sided 11%-13% comfort range, using its upper bound as the single quantitative ceiling since the schema has no two-sided range operator with distinct bounds.

promise.statement: CEO K Krithivasan stated that, while TCS does not give specific numeric guidance, management was "more optimistic" about international revenue for the coming quarter (Q2 FY2026).
promise.originalExcerpt: Nitin, as you know, we don't give any specific guidance, but on the international revenue part, we are more optimistic in the coming quarter.

outcome.explanation: TCS's official Q2 FY2026 results press release reported international revenue grew 0.6% QoQ in constant currency, confirming the directional optimism management expressed on the prior quarter's call. Since the original statement was explicitly qualitative/directional (management stated it does not give numeric guidance), any reported sequential growth in international revenue is classified as ACHIEVED rather than measured against a specific numeric target.

promiseEvidence.sourceTitle: Transcript of the Earnings Conference Call for the Quarter Ended June 30, 2025 (BSE Filing TCS/SE/71/2025-26)
promiseEvidence.excerpt: Nitin, as you know, we don't give any specific guidance, but on the international revenue part, we are more optimistic in the coming quarter.

outcomeEvidence.sourceTitle: Press Release: TCS Q2 FY 2025-26 Financial Results (NSE Filing TCS/BM/SE/118/2025-26)
outcomeEvidence.excerpt: International Revenue grows 0.6% QoQ in Constant Currency

verification.notes: Promise sourced from the official BSE-filed transcript; outcome sourced from the official NSE-filed press-release letter (both fetched directly from the exchange archives, since tcs.com itself currently blocks direct fetching with a Cloudflare managed challenge). This is a qualitative/directional promise -- TCS explicitly does not give numeric guidance -- so ACHIEVED reflects that the direction management expressed (optimism about improving international revenue) matched the subsequently reported direction (positive QoQ growth), not a match against a specific numeric target.
